summary: Per-residue binary prediction of which residues are catalytic active-site residues.
what_it_measures: For each residue in a protein, a 0/1 label for whether it is an annotated active site. Labels come from Swiss-Prot 'Active site' sequence features (1-based positions expanded to a per-residue binary vector).
assay_method: Expert-curated active-site annotations in Swiss-Prot, based on experimental and homology evidence.
provenance: Parsed from the Swiss-Prot `active_site` feature column into residue-position vectors; the model keeps the full per-residue embedding tensor.
when_to_use: A residue-level localization task testing whether embeddings pinpoint catalytic machinery; relevant to mechanism annotation and active-site design.
caveats: Extremely imbalanced: 0.39% of the residues in the dataset are annotated, so a model that predicts no site anywhere scores above 99% accuracy. AUPRC is the primary metric for that reason. Swiss-Prot annotation coverage is incomplete and many annotations were propagated by homology.

citations.title: UniProt: the Universal Protein Knowledgebase in 2025
